To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
active passive design is superior to active design.

the active passive design configuration using shear piezoelectrical actuators embedded in the viscoelastic core of the sandwich beam is the best design configuration for the active passive damping of cantilever beams.

(1) active passive damping design configuration using extension piezoelectrics with viscoelastic treatments is the best performing design configuration; (2) the active passive damping design using shear mode piezoelectronics and viscoelastic treatments provides a good performance; and (3) active passive damping designs using extension piezotronics with viscoelastic materials provide a good damping performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with

experimental analysis of active passive damping design configuration using extension piezoelectrics combined with constrained layer treatments, shear piezoelectronics embedded in a sandwich structure and purely active configuration.
the experimental investigation of the performance of three active-passive damping treatments applied to a cantilver beam.
the design and experimental analysis of a novel hybrid active passive damping treatment based on the use of shear piezoelectrics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the active passive design configuration with shear mode piezoelectric sensors and actuators is the most efficient and effective design configuration.
the best active passive design configuration depends on the application, and it should be selected based on the specific design criteria and requirements of the system.

the active passive design configurations based on extension piezoelectrics are more effective than the active passive design based on shear piezoelectronics and that both active passive design configurations outperform the purely active design configuration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hybrid active passive designs are very effective and reliable in reducing vibrations and noise.

the hybrid active passive design configuration with extension mode actuators bonded on top of viscoelastic constrained damping layer treatments is the best design configuration for active passive damping of beams and plates.
the active passive design with extension piezoelectrics and constrained layer damping treatments provides the best damping performance and robustness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the active passive damping performance depends mainly on the design configuration and not on the specific type of piezoelectrics and viscoelastic materials used.

the hybrid active passive damping treatments are more robust, reliable and provide wider range damping than purely active damping treatments and that they should be considered as an alternative to purely active control in many applications.
the active passive design configurations based on extension piezoelectrics are more robust and provide wider range damping than the shear piezoelectronic configuration.
